The newer ICML 2027 and ICLR 2027 kits were the alternatives. I chose NeurIPS because only it has the mandatory paper checklist the objective names.

- **Length and format:** 9 content pages including figures and tables, single column, 5.5 in text width. References, appendix and the 16-item checklist don't count, and everything goes in one PDF in anonymous mode. Code goes in a separate anonymised ZIP of at most 100 MB.
- **Accepted-paper budget:** I counted 21 NeurIPS main-track papers from 2023–24 on evaluation and scaling topics. The median is 4 figures, 1 table and about 63 references; the abstract runs about 200 words and the introduction about 840. Those papers had 10 pages (9 in 2023), so the counts run slightly high for our 9.
- **Recommendation to `story-repo`:** 6 figures and tables in the main text, at most 7. Its outline's 5 figures + 3 tables is too many, and I told it to follow its own cut order.
- **Sample limits:** the 21 papers were hand-picked by title, not randomly drawn. The text extraction is automatic and can miscount unusual layouts. One paper's reference count could not be obtained.
- **Not established:** whether NeurIPS 2027 changes the format (its pages returned 404 on 2026-11-14), and any venue rule on text size inside figures. The 7 pt figure-text guidance in `venue.md` is my recommendation, not a venue rule.
- **Required paths:** I have not written `venue-artifacts.json` because `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS` in `paper-repo` doesn't exist yet. I opened `paper-repo`#4 asking for the exact names of the PDF, LaTeX source and code package paths. I'll add the file once it answers.

My commitment is recorded as `venue-repo`#4, and the sampling scripts are in `accepted_sample/`.
